mechanism: Compare all four homologous outer ear tips (red) and all four inner ear tips (blue) with the two diagonal candidate axes. Predict an overgeneralization from repeated ear-feature organization to both diagonal symmetries, adding the two diagonals to the two actual midline symmetries, hence 4. Unlike old diagonal-corner tip grouping, color groups here are anatomical feature types and each group is itself invariant under both true reflections.
primary_math_proof: There are exactly four displayed candidate lines: x=0, y=0, y=x, y=-x. Each of the 400 upper-left head segments is copied with independent sign changes to produce all four heads. Thus reflecting the entire segment set in x=0 or y=0 preserves it. The eye point (-0.69,0.55), for example, and snout/ear geometry do not map to the same anatomical set under diagonal exchange. More decisive exhaustive segment-set comparison and an explicit positive-distance witness against each diagonal are saved in proof_calculation.json. Every segment is considered, not just the four tips. Both diagonal failures and both valid midlines exhaust the candidates. The added red tip set is {(+-0.96,+-0.98)} and blue tip set {(+-0.34,+-0.98)}; each is invariant under x and y reflection. Consequently even if these endpoint marks are intrinsic ink, both true symmetries still work. Added ink cannot repair a geometric nonoverlap; positive-distance witnesses remain outside marked tips. Unique answer remains 2.

Candidate fold-line colors are on the preexisting comparison guides, not a requirement to match a different animal. Full snouts, inner ears, eyes and necks remain exposed; native PNG review required.

New design introduces a second real anatomical feature family, groups each family across ALL FOUR heads, and preserves horizontal/vertical colored symmetry. This changes correspondence membership and the human material-color calculation, beyond a palette or linewidth change.
